children: Nvidia has formed a board committee to oversee national security and export controls after founder Jensen Huang resigned over an affair with a woman U.S. officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence.

The company said Tuesday that its new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will oversee national security policies, compliance with export controls and risks related to global trade.

Director Suzanne Nora Johnson will chair the committee, which will meet at least quarterly. Nvidia's national security and global trade compliance teams will report directly to the committee and the interim chief executive Colette Kress.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Nvidia board Chairman Harvey Jones said.
The move follows Huang's resignation last week and a proposed Commerce Department rule that would tighten restrictions on shipments of chips from Nvidia and other U.S. companies.

The proposal would add Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil to a list of countries subject to export restrictions. Companies would need Commerce Department licenses to ship chips to those countries, though U.S. technology companies could qualify for exceptions.
The proposed restrictions aim to prevent Chinese customers from remotely accessing data-center capacity in those countries.
